_readme: Authoritative Local generation catalog. Templates own their reasoning prompt and typed slots. Assessment points define what may be tested and the difficulty range after variables are bound.

evidence_types.name: Module Graph
evidence_types.description: Source modules and their high-level organisation.

evidence_types.name: Data Flow
evidence_types.description: Functions and paths that move or transform data.

evidence_types.name: Control Flow
evidence_types.description: Functions and paths containing branches, loops, and state changes.

evidence_types.name: Symbol Table
evidence_types.description: Declared classes, functions, methods, and module-level symbols.

evidence_types.name: Complexity Analysis
evidence_types.description: Heuristic function-size, loop, branch, and call indicators.

evidence_types.name: Test Discovery
evidence_types.description: Discovered test files and test-like functions.

evidence_types.name: API Discovery
evidence_types.description: Routes, endpoints, requests, responses, and external communication.

evidence_types.name: SQL Analysis
evidence_types.description: SQL files, statements, schemas, and persistence operations.

assessment_points.name: Package Purpose
assessment_points.description: Why an imported Python package is present and what it contributes to this project.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify the general purpose of a common package.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain a package's evidenced, project-specific use.

assessment_points.query: python package library import dependency purpose project use

assessment_points.name: Module / Component Responsibility
assessment_points.description: The responsibility, boundary, and downstream contribution of a module or component.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a named module or component.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain its direct project responsibility.
difficulty_anchors.3: Relate its responsibility to another component or downstream effect.

assessment_points.query: module component responsibility boundary role downstream

assessment_points.name: Function Input / Output Contract
assessment_points.description: A function's accepted inputs, returned structure, side effects, and caller expectations.

difficulty_anchors.1: Read an explicit parameter or return form.
difficulty_anchors.2: Infer the concrete input or output structure from the function body.
difficulty_anchors.3: Explain the contract's effect on a caller or downstream stage.

assessment_points.query: function parameter input return output type format side effect caller

assessment_points.name: Data Source / Acquisition
assessment_points.description: Where data originates and how Python retrieves, loads, or scrapes it.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify the source, file, API, or acquisition library.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain request parameters and the retrieved format.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace pagination, batching, quota, or repeated acquisition behavior.

assessment_points.query: data source acquire retrieve load scrape api request file pagination batch quota

assessment_points.name: External Interface Contract
assessment_points.description: API endpoints, MQTT topics, request/response payloads, and producer-consumer expectations.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify an endpoint, topic, method, or payload field.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace the contract between producer and consumer.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse the consequence of a contract or payload change.

assessment_points.query: api endpoint mqtt topic request response payload producer consumer contract

assessment_points.name: Data Format / Structure
assessment_points.description: The fields, types, shapes, and conversions of CSV, JSON, DataFrame, and record structures.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a data format, field, or basic structure.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain a format or type conversion.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace how a structural mismatch affects a downstream operation.

assessment_points.query: csv json dataframe record field column type format schema conversion

assessment_points.name: Cleaning / Missing Values
assessment_points.description: Deduplication, filtering, null handling, type correction, and consistency rules.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a cleaning operation used by the project.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain the rule applied to invalid, duplicate, or missing data.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict the cleaned result for a concrete input.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse a faulty cleaning policy or an unhandled anomaly.

assessment_points.query: clean filter missing null deduplicate duplicate type convert inconsistent invalid

assessment_points.name: Transformation / Aggregation
assessment_points.description: How records are mapped, grouped, aggregated, reshaped, or reduced to a new grain.

difficulty_anchors.2: Explain the direct purpose of a transformation.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict the transformed values, shape, or aggregation grain.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose an incorrect transformation or aggregation result.

assessment_points.query: transform map group aggregate reshape grain calculate dataframe

assessment_points.name: Integration / Entity Matching
assessment_points.description: How datasets are joined and how records, facilities, units, or identifiers are matched.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify the join or matching key.
difficulty_anchors.3: Explain how two project datasets are integrated.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse unmatched, duplicated, or wrong-grain integration results.

assessment_points.query: integrate join merge match identifier facility unit key grain

assessment_points.name: Data Augmentation / Enrichment
assessment_points.description: How external attributes such as geolocation are acquired, matched, and added to existing records.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify the enrichment source and added attribute.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace how enrichment data is matched and attached.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse incomplete matches, API failures, or enrichment quality.

assessment_points.query: augment enrich geocode geocoding latitude longitude location coordinates external attribute match

assessment_points.name: Pipeline / Data Flow
assessment_points.description: The order and direction of data movement across acquisition, processing, storage, publishing, and presentation.

difficulty_anchors.2: Trace one direct source-to-destination step.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace a multi-stage workflow and intermediate forms.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse a cross-component consequence or broken pipeline path.

assessment_points.query: pipeline workflow data flow source destination stage order intermediate extraction validation storage visualisation visualization

assessment_points.name: Persistence / Schema Integrity
assessment_points.description: Tables, keys, relationships, constraints, persistence operations, and stored data grain.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a table, column, or persistence technology.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain a table's purpose or a basic key constraint.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace how records are written and related at the intended grain.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse a schema, constraint, or integrity failure.

assessment_points.query: database table column primary key foreign key constraint persist sql grain integrity

assessment_points.name: Caching / Materialisation
assessment_points.description: Why intermediate data is persisted and how caching limits repeated retrieval or processing.

difficulty_anchors.2: Explain why a cached file or materialised dataset exists.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace when cached versus fresh data is used.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse stale data, invalidation, or unnecessary repeated work.

assessment_points.query: cache materialize csv persist reuse refresh stale invalidation api calls

assessment_points.name: Streaming / Event Behaviour
assessment_points.description: Publishing, subscribing, event-time order, message delay, delta detection, and continuous execution.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify publisher, subscriber, topic, or message direction.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace ordered or delta-only streaming behaviour.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse duplicate, stale, out-of-order, or continuously repeated events.

assessment_points.query: mqtt publish subscribe stream event order delay delta continuous message

assessment_points.name: Condition / State Behaviour
assessment_points.description: Observable branch outcomes, state changes, loop behaviour, and shared runtime state.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify the direct outcome of a visible condition.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict multiple assignments, calls, or state changes along a path.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse state-dependent behaviour across functions or iterations.

assessment_points.query: condition branch loop state assignment return side effect outcome

assessment_points.name: Failure Handling / Recovery
assessment_points.description: Exceptions, retries, timeout handling, fallback paths, cleanup, and recovery behaviour.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify an exception, guard, retry, or cleanup action.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict the behaviour of an evidenced failure path.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose an incomplete or harmful recovery path.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate a recovery design across API, storage, or streaming boundaries.

assessment_points.query: error exception timeout retry fallback cleanup recovery failure

assessment_points.name: Configuration / Security / Validation
assessment_points.description: Environment configuration, secrets, input validation, authentication, authorization, and safe handling.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a configuration source or protected value.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain how configuration or validation is used by one component.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace a validated or rejected input through the project.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse the consequence of missing validation, exposed secrets, or incorrect authorization.

assessment_points.query: environment config secret token validate authenticate authorize sanitize input

assessment_points.name: Testing / Data Quality Verification
assessment_points.description: Tests, assertions, quality checks, expected behaviour, and uncovered edge cases.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify what a test or quality check verifies.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict whether a concrete input satisfies the verified behaviour.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse missing coverage or select a test that exposes a fault.

assessment_points.query: test assertion fixture expected quality check edge case coverage

assessment_points.name: Performance / Scalability
assessment_points.description: Repeated work, algorithmic cost, resource use, throughput, and project bottlenecks.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify repeated work, a loop, or a resource-heavy operation.
difficulty_anchors.3: Explain the direct performance effect at the project's expected scale.
difficulty_anchors.4: Locate and reason about a measured or evidenced bottleneck.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate an optimisation and its correctness or resource trade-off.

assessment_points.query: performance complexity scale memory throughput repeated work bottleneck optimize

assessment_points.name: Design Decision / Change Impact
assessment_points.description: Why a design is used, what trade-offs it carries, and how a requirement change affects the system.

difficulty_anchors.3: Explain the project-specific rationale for a local design choice.
difficulty_anchors.4: Compare alternatives or trace the impact of a cross-component change.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate a system-level trade-off and propose an evidence-consistent design.

assessment_points.query: design decision rationale tradeoff alternative requirement change impact architecture

assessment_points.name: Module Dependency / Boundary
assessment_points.description: How modules are separated, which direction dependencies run, and which boundary owns an interaction.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify a direct module dependency or boundary.
difficulty_anchors.3: Explain why a responsibility belongs on one side of the boundary.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse coupling or the consequence of changing the dependency direction.

assessment_points.query: module dependency boundary coupling layer separation import direction interface

assessment_points.name: Entrypoint / Application Lifecycle
assessment_points.description: How execution starts, initializes resources, coordinates stages, and shuts down.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify an entrypoint or initialization function.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain the direct startup or shutdown sequence.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace lifecycle-dependent calls and state.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse a faulty initialization, cleanup, or ordering change.

assessment_points.query: entrypoint main startup initialize lifecycle shutdown cleanup bootstrap run application

assessment_points.name: Configuration / Deployment
assessment_points.description: How runtime settings, environments, paths, and deployment-specific values alter project behaviour.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a configuration source or environment setting.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain where one runtime value is consumed.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace how configuration changes project behaviour.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse an environment-specific configuration failure.

assessment_points.query: configuration environment variable setting deployment path host port runtime dotenv

assessment_points.name: Request / Response Handling
assessment_points.description: How requests are constructed and how status, headers, payloads, and errors are interpreted.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a request method or response field.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain request construction or response parsing.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace a response into downstream project data.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse incorrect status, payload, or error handling.

assessment_points.query: http request response status header body payload parse client get post error

assessment_points.name: Pagination / Rate Limits
assessment_points.description: How an integration retrieves multiple pages and respects quotas, throttling, or backoff constraints.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify a page token, limit, or quota.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace repeated retrieval across pages.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse missing records or excessive calls caused by pagination logic.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate a quota-safe pagination and backoff design.

assessment_points.query: pagination page cursor offset limit quota rate throttle backoff api repeated request

assessment_points.name: Retry / Idempotency
assessment_points.description: Whether repeated external operations are safe and how retry behaviour avoids duplicated effects.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify a retry or repeatable operation.
difficulty_anchors.3: Explain the observable effect of repeating it.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose duplicate writes, messages, or requests.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate an idempotency mechanism across components.

assessment_points.query: retry idempotent duplicate repeated request write message backoff operation safe

assessment_points.name: Orchestration / Scheduling
assessment_points.description: How jobs, tasks, dependencies, triggers, and execution schedules coordinate a workflow.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a scheduled job or task.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain a direct task dependency or trigger.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace an ordered multi-task run.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse a scheduling, dependency, or rerun failure.

assessment_points.query: orchestration schedule scheduler cron dag task dependency trigger job workflow run airflow

assessment_points.name: Ordering / Deduplication
assessment_points.description: How records or events are sorted, keyed, de-duplicated, and processed in a stable order.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify an ordering or duplicate-removal key.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict the retained order and records.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse stale, repeated, or out-of-order results.

assessment_points.query: order sort sequence deduplicate duplicate unique key timestamp stable event record

assessment_points.name: Window / Buffer Processing
assessment_points.description: How streams or collections are partitioned into windows, buffers, batches, or time intervals.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify the window, buffer, or batch boundary.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict which records are processed together.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse late, partial, or boundary records.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate a windowing trade-off for latency and correctness.

assessment_points.query: window buffer batch chunk interval event time tumbling sliding latency records

assessment_points.name: Data Lineage / Quality
assessment_points.description: How provenance, quality rules, and intermediate checks connect an output to its source.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify a source or quality check for an output.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace a value through transformations and checks.
difficulty_anchors.4: Locate where an invalid output could enter the lineage.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate whether the available checks establish trustworthy lineage.

assessment_points.query: data lineage provenance quality source trace audit intermediate validation output origin

assessment_points.name: Algorithm / Control Logic
assessment_points.description: The ordered steps, branches, loops, and termination conditions that implement a local algorithm.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a visible step or branch.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain the purpose of a short control path.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace an input through several steps.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose incorrect ordering or termination.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate correctness across interacting paths and edge cases.

assessment_points.query: algorithm logic steps branch loop iteration termination condition calculate control path

assessment_points.name: State Mutation / Side Effect
assessment_points.description: How functions mutate shared state or produce externally observable effects beyond returning a value.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify a state change or side effect.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace the effect to a later read or caller.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse an unexpected mutation or ordering dependency.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate a safer state-management design.

assessment_points.query: state mutation side effect global assignment update shared variable write caller

assessment_points.name: Resource Lifecycle
assessment_points.description: How files, connections, clients, threads, and other resources are opened, used, and released.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify resource acquisition or cleanup.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace the complete resource lifecycle.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose a leak or incomplete cleanup path.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate lifecycle safety across failures or concurrency.

assessment_points.query: resource lifecycle open close connect disconnect file client thread cleanup context manager

assessment_points.name: Edge Case / Boundary Behaviour
assessment_points.description: Observable behaviour for empty, missing, extreme, malformed, or boundary inputs.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify a guarded boundary condition.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict behaviour for one concrete edge input.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose an unhandled boundary case.
difficulty_anchors.5: Reason across interacting edge cases and recovery paths.

assessment_points.query: edge case boundary empty missing malformed invalid zero negative maximum minimum input

assessment_points.name: Entity Relationship / Keys
assessment_points.description: How entities relate and how primary, foreign, natural, or composite keys identify records.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify an entity, relationship, or key.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain cardinality or key purpose.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace how related records are linked.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse an incorrect key or relationship design.

assessment_points.query: entity relationship primary foreign composite natural key cardinality one many model

assessment_points.name: Query / Join / Filter Semantics
assessment_points.description: Which records a database query selects, joins, groups, orders, or excludes.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a queried table or filter.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain a direct query clause.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict the result set or join output.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose incorrect, missing, or duplicated rows.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate a complex query's correctness and grain.

assessment_points.query: sql query select where filter join group by having order result rows semantics

assessment_points.name: Transaction / Atomicity
assessment_points.description: How grouped persistence operations commit, roll back, and preserve consistency under failure.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify a transaction boundary or commit.
difficulty_anchors.3: Explain which writes succeed or roll back together.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse a partial-write or concurrency failure.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate an atomicity or isolation design.

assessment_points.query: transaction atomicity commit rollback isolation consistency partial write insert all writes together failure stored database

assessment_points.name: Schema Evolution / Migration
assessment_points.description: How stored structures and consumers adapt when fields, types, tables, or versions change.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify a schema version or structural change.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace the direct migration effect.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse compatibility or data-loss risk.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate a safe staged migration across producers and consumers.

assessment_points.query: schema evolution migration version alter table backward compatibility field type change

assessment_points.name: Authentication / Authorization
assessment_points.description: How identities are established and how permissions restrict protected operations or data.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify an authentication credential or protected operation.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain an access check.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace an accepted or rejected request.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose an access-control flaw.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate authorization boundaries across components.

assessment_points.query: authentication authorization identity login token session role permission access control protected

assessment_points.name: Input Validation / Injection
assessment_points.description: How untrusted input is validated, encoded, parameterised, or rejected before sensitive use.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify an input validation or parameterisation step.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace valid and invalid input paths.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose an injection or unsafe-input flaw.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate validation across API, command, and database boundaries.

assessment_points.query: input validation sanitize injection sql command parameterized untrusted encode reject

assessment_points.name: Secrets / Sensitive Data
assessment_points.description: How credentials and sensitive values are stored, transmitted, logged, and prevented from exposure.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a secret or sensitive value.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain how it is loaded or protected.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace where it may be transmitted or logged.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose an exposure path.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate protection across storage, transport, and observability.

assessment_points.query: secret credential password api key token sensitive data privacy log expose encrypt environment

assessment_points.name: Test Scope / Isolation
assessment_points.description: Whether unit, integration, and end-to-end tests isolate dependencies at the intended boundary.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a test type or dependency double.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain what the test isolates.
difficulty_anchors.3: Distinguish unit, integration, and end-to-end coverage.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse a misleading mock or incorrect test boundary.

assessment_points.query: unit integration end to end test isolation mock stub fake fixture dependency boundary

assessment_points.name: Boundary / Failure Testing
assessment_points.description: Tests that verify invalid, empty, extreme, exceptional, and recovery behaviour.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify a boundary or failure test.
difficulty_anchors.3: Select a test input that reaches a guarded path.
difficulty_anchors.4: Design a test that exposes an unhandled fault.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate failure coverage across component boundaries.

assessment_points.query: boundary failure test exception invalid empty extreme timeout recovery edge case assertion

assessment_points.name: Time / Space Complexity
assessment_points.description: How input size affects operation count and memory use for evidenced code paths.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify a loop, collection, or repeated operation.
difficulty_anchors.3: Determine a local time or space growth rate.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse nested work or materialisation at scale.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate a complexity improvement without changing correctness.

assessment_points.query: time space complexity big o input size nested loop memory allocation growth algorithm

assessment_points.name: Object Design Principles
assessment_points.description: How classes preserve invariants, encapsulate state, and divide responsibilities.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a class, field, or method.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain an encapsulated responsibility.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace how a method preserves object state.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose poor cohesion or broken invariants.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate a responsibility or interface redesign.

assessment_points.query: object oriented class encapsulation invariant responsibility cohesion solid method state

assessment_points.name: Class Collaboration / Polymorphism
assessment_points.description: How objects collaborate through composition, inheritance, interfaces, and substitutable behaviour.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify a class relationship or overridden method.
difficulty_anchors.3: Explain a collaboration or dispatch path.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse composition versus inheritance in the evidenced design.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate substitutability and extension impact across classes.

assessment_points.query: class collaboration composition inheritance interface abstraction polymorphism override dispatch object

templates.name: Contextual Use
templates.reasoning_prompt: Identify the immediate, project-specific role of one subject using the supplied evidence.
stem_frames: In {context}, which statement correctly describes what {subject} does in this project?
In {context}, which statement correctly describes how the project uses {subject}?
templates.option_task: Test only the subject's immediate, project-specific role. Do not test a multi-stage flow, ordering, or downstream consequences. Do not test generic library knowledge or repeat what its name suggests.
templates.query: project-specific use interaction input output side effect dependency

required.label: concrete usage
required.query: import call use publish subscribe request transform save table

templates.name: Interaction / Flow
templates.reasoning_prompt: Trace an evidenced relationship, data path, or code path involving at least two entities.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes how {subject} and {counterpart} work together?
Which statement correctly describes the link from {subject} to {counterpart}?
Which statement correctly describes what moves from {subject} to {counterpart}?
templates.option_task: Test a relationship involving at least two entities, including evidenced direction, ordering, transferred data, or downstream consequence. Every option must be a complete relational claim.
templates.query: workflow order interaction source destination call flow dependency

required.label: evidenced relationship
required.query: source destination call order data flow dependency

templates.name: Condition / Outcome
templates.reasoning_prompt: Determine an observable outcome from the shown condition and code.
stem_frames: In the code below, what happens when {condition}?
templates.option_task: State exact calls, assignments, output, exceptions, or return behavior visible in the complete shown branch.
templates.query: condition branch state outcome exception return side effect

required.label: conditional code
required.query: if else try except match return set update

templates.name: Code Explain
templates.reasoning_prompt: Explain the complete evidenced effect of the shown code.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes what the code below does?
templates.option_task: Test the complete visible effect, including material calls, transformations, state changes, and return behavior.
templates.query: implementation effect transformation state return code

templates.name: Fault / Correction
templates.reasoning_prompt: Reason about one explicit hypothetical change and the behavior it would break.
stem_frames: A developer changes the code to {mutation}. Which statement correctly describes the problem this causes and how to fix it?
templates.option_task: Exactly one option must pair the observable consequence of the explicit hypothetical mutation with the correction that restores the shown behavior. Do not claim the original code is faulty.
templates.query: hypothetical change consequence correction condition return call

templates.name: Requirement / Change
templates.reasoning_prompt: Choose a change that meets a concrete requirement while preserving shown behavior.
stem_frames: The code must {requirement}. Which option should be added at INSERT HERE without changing the current behavior?
templates.option_task: Each option must be a short syntactically plausible snippet for the marked location. Exactly one must satisfy the stated requirement and preserve the visible control/data flow.
templates.query: requirement insert extend log validate preserve behavior

templates.name: Constraint / Verification
templates.reasoning_prompt: Explain a concrete, evidenced constraint or verified behaviour.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes the rule for {subject}?
Which statement correctly describes the checked behavior of {subject}?
templates.option_task: Test a concrete schema rule, validation guard, test expectation, security condition, data-quality rule, or measured complexity indicator. Do not ask for an undocumented design preference.
templates.query: constraint validation assertion schema integrity guard complexity

required.label: verifiable constraint
required.query: constraint not null primary key assertion validate guard loop branch

templates.name: Approach Used
templates.reasoning_prompt: Identify the project approach shown by the supplied evidence.
stem_frames: In {context}, which statement correctly describes the approach used for {subject}?
templates.option_task: Describe the actual project approach, such as batch loading, repeated polling, caching, streaming, or background processing. Do not test only a general definition.
templates.query: approach method batch polling cache streaming background process

required.label: project approach
required.query: load fetch poll cache publish subscribe save process

templates.name: Data Flow Selection
templates.reasoning_prompt: Choose the project data flow that matches the supplied evidence.
stem_frames: Which flow correctly shows how data moves from {source} to {destination}?
templates.option_task: Each option must be a complete ordered flow. Use clear arrows and include only stages supported by the evidence.
templates.query: data flow source stage destination order pipeline

required.label: ordered data flow
required.query: source destination stage order data moves

templates.name: Source and Method
templates.reasoning_prompt: Match a project data source or service with the way the project uses it.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly matches {subject} with the way it gets or sends data?
templates.option_task: Match the named source, service, or component with its real method, such as an API request, file load, database query, publish, or subscribe action.
templates.query: source method api request file load query publish subscribe

required.label: source and method
required.query: request read load query publish subscribe

templates.name: Stage Responsibility
templates.reasoning_prompt: Identify the job of a project stage or component from the supplied evidence.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes the job of {subject} in the data process?
templates.option_task: Describe what the stage receives, does, and passes on. Keep each option focused on one clear project responsibility.
templates.query: stage component responsibility input process output pipeline

templates.name: Processing Mode
templates.reasoning_prompt: Identify how the project processes data over time.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes how {subject} processes data?
templates.option_task: Describe the evidenced mode in simple terms, such as one-time batch work, repeated polling, cached replay, continuous messages, or background updates.
templates.query: batch repeated polling continuous stream replay background loop delay

required.label: processing mode
required.query: loop repeat delay batch stream publish subscribe

templates.name: Data Grain
templates.reasoning_prompt: Identify what one project record or message represents.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes what one record in {subject} represents?
templates.option_task: State the unit represented by one row, record, or message, including keys such as facility, unit, region, or time when the evidence supports them.
templates.query: record row message grain facility unit region timestamp key

required.label: record structure
required.query: record row field key facility unit region time

templates.name: State / Output Trace
templates.reasoning_prompt: Execute the complete shown path and determine the final state, output, return value, and material side effects.
stem_frames: After the shown code runs, which statement correctly describes the resulting state and output?
templates.option_task: Each option must give a concrete final result. Exactly one must match every visible assignment, call, branch, output, exception, and return; do not require hidden code or memorisation.
templates.query: trace execute final state variable output return side effect path

required.label: complete executable path
required.query: assignment branch loop return print update append

templates.name: Edge-case Outcome
templates.reasoning_prompt: Determine the exact observable behaviour for one concrete boundary or invalid input using the complete shown path.
stem_frames: When {condition}, which statement correctly describes the evidenced behaviour?
templates.option_task: Use one concrete empty, missing, malformed, extreme, timeout, or failure condition. Exactly one option must match the shown guard, exception, fallback, state change, and return behaviour.
templates.query: edge case empty missing invalid boundary exception fallback outcome

required.label: guarded boundary path
required.query: if empty none missing invalid except timeout return

templates.name: Test Case Selection
templates.reasoning_prompt: Choose the test setup and assertion that objectively verifies one evidenced behaviour or exposes one evidenced fault.
stem_frames: Which test case correctly verifies the required behaviour of {subject}?
templates.option_task: Each option must specify an input or setup and an observable assertion. Exactly one must exercise the requested path and assert its evidenced result; avoid subjective claims about which test is better.
templates.query: test case input setup assertion expected failure boundary verify behavior

required.label: testable behaviour
required.query: assert expected return error validate boundary

templates.name: Contract Verification
templates.reasoning_prompt: Verify one concrete input, output, payload, schema, permission, or transaction contract against the supplied evidence.
stem_frames: Which statement satisfies the evidenced contract for {subject}?
templates.option_task: Exactly one option must satisfy every evidenced field, type, key, status, permission, or atomicity rule. Incorrect options must contradict a visible contract rather than represent merely weaker designs.
templates.query: contract input output schema payload field status key permission transaction satisfy

required.label: explicit contract
required.query: parameter return payload field type key constraint status assert

templates.name: Complexity Analysis
templates.reasoning_prompt: Determine an evidenced time, space, I/O, or throughput implication and its cause.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes the evidenced complexity or resource behaviour of {subject}?
templates.option_task: Exactly one option must match the visible loops, calls, allocations, materialisation, or repeated I/O. Do not assert an exact Big-O class unless the shown path supports it.
templates.query: complexity time space memory io throughput repeated loop allocation scale

required.label: resource indicator
required.query: loop branch call repeated load write memory size

templates.name: Dependency Change Impact
templates.reasoning_prompt: Trace the objectively evidenced effect of changing one module, interface, schema, or dependency.
stem_frames: Which evidenced part directly depends on {subject} and would therefore require review if its contract changed?
templates.option_task: Exactly one option must follow a visible dependency, call, data-flow, API, or schema edge. Do not ask which design is better or rely on undocumented architectural intent.
templates.query: change impact dependency caller consumer schema interface downstream affected

required.label: dependency edge
required.query: depends calls consumes imports reads writes downstream
